feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so it states no outcome for it. Iteration 3 (wheel_track 0.09 m, kp 1.5, kd 0.25) is the best so far at 57.9: s-bend progress rose from 0.163 to 0.178 and slalom stayed flat, while max_error stayed at the 0.063 m floor on the s-bend and every run ended off_track. The s-bend already shows steering_oscillation 0.169, above the 0.15 caution level. Iteration 2 showed that lighter, shorter bodies and a forward sensor lead (y=0.07) both cost points, so keep y=0.05 and mass 0.8 kg. Iteration 1 showed slalom line loss of 1.0 per run, which is still present. For the wheel_track 0.08 m step, I have scaled kp down to 1.35 so that the yaw gain per unit of differential matches iteration 3. That means the next race reads the track change at roughly matched controller gain. When the race reports: if s-bend progress rises above 0.18 and steering_oscillation stays at or below about 0.17, the narrower track is helping and you can keep 0.08 m. If oscillation rises above about 0.2 or the first off-track event comes earlier on the s-bend, the turn is overshooting, so return to 0.09 m. If progress stays near 0.18 with max_error still at the 0.06 m floor, the limit is ground speed, not turn rate.
requested_changes: Keep wheel_track at 0.08 m only if the next race shows s-bend progress above 0.18 and steering_oscillation at or below about 0.17. Evidence: iteration 3 (0.09 m) gave s-bend progress 0.178 and oscillation 0.169; iteration 1 to 3 showed that narrowing the track was the only geometry change that raised the score.

If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2 or the s-bend off-track event comes earlier, return wheel_track to 0.09 m and raise mass from 0.8 kg to 0.9 kg before changing sensors. Evidence: iteration 2's lighter body (0.6 kg) cut s-bend progress from 0.163 to 0.119, so extra inertia is the safer damping lever.

If progress stays near 0.18 with max_error still at 0.06 m on the s-bend and slalom, change wheel_radius from 0.03 m to 0.035 m for more ground speed, keeping the track width of whichever value survives. Evidence: iterations 1 and 3 kept progress between 0.11 and 0.18 with no sign that turn rate alone is the limit.
